title: Two Views of Peronism: Sin Embargo and No Obstante

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *sin embargo* from A2 Unit 28 and *no obstante* (a little more formal) from B1 Unit 1. Both open the second half of a sentence that goes against the first half. Peronism is a topic where supporters and critics disagree, so these connectors help you put two views side by side without taking sides.

sections.title: Contrast connectors
rows: Perón tenía el apoyo de los sindicatos; sin embargo, sus críticos decían que limitaba la prensa.
*sin embargo*: however (the second view goes against the first)
Se ampliaron los derechos laborales; no obstante, la oposición desconfiaba del gobierno.
El peronismo fue prohibido en 1955; sin embargo, siguió vivo entre los obreros.
contrast: what happened is the opposite of what was expected
Evita murió en 1952; no obstante, su figura sigue presente.
contrast: a loss, then something that continues

items.spanish: Perón tenía el apoyo de los sindicatos; sin embargo, sus críticos decían que limitaba la prensa.
items.english: Perón had the support of the unions; however, his critics said he limited the press.

items.spanish: Se ampliaron los derechos laborales; no obstante, la oposición desconfiaba del gobierno.
items.english: Labour rights were extended; nevertheless, the opposition distrusted the government.

items.spanish: El peronismo fue prohibido en 1955; sin embargo, siguió vivo entre los obreros.
items.english: Peronism was banned in 1955; however, it stayed alive among workers.

items.spanish: Evita murió en 1952; no obstante, su figura sigue presente.
items.english: Evita died in 1952; nevertheless, her figure is still present.

sections.content: A semicolon or a full stop comes before the connector and a comma after it: *…; sin embargo, …*. Use a contrast connector only when the second idea goes against the first. For a result, use *por eso* or *así que*. When you report a political view, say whose view it is (*sus críticos decían*, *sus partidarios creen*).
